meta.title: Ocean Explorer
meta.description: Ocean Explorer: dive from the surface to the deepest trench.

descent.label: The descent
descent.title: Breaking the surface
descent.text: The sky folds into a ripple of light overhead. With every metre, the sea takes a little more of the sun.
descent.textNight: The night sky folds into a ripple of silver overhead. Below you, the water is already dark.

shallows.label: Shallow water
shallows.title: Cathedral light
shallows.text: Shafts of sun lean through the blue. Red light is long gone; below 200 metres only blue still reaches you.
shallows.textNight: Faint moonbeams lean through the dark blue. Here and there, plankton sparks as you pass.

glow.label: Bioluminescence
glow.title: Living light
glow.text: Out of the dark, jellyfish pulse with their own light. Most animals down here make it: to hunt, to hide, to find each other.

whale.label: Whale encounter
whale.title: A passing giant
whale.text: A sperm whale hunts in total darkness, finding squid by sound alone. One breath at the surface lasts it over an hour.

vents.label: Hydrothermal vents
vents.title: Black smokers
vents.text: Water hotter than 350 °C pours out of the seafloor, thick with minerals. Life thrives here without any sunlight at all.

abyss.label: The abyss
abyss.title: The abyss
abyss.text: The deepest water on Earth, under more than a thousand times the pressure of the air above. Something vast moves at the edge of the light, and is gone.

return.label: Return to surface
return.title: Back into the light
return.text: Eleven kilometres of water above you, and every metre a little brighter than the last.

end.title: The ocean is still unexplored
end.note: More than eighty percent of the ocean has never been mapped, observed or explored.
